title: Humatics evidence extraction
summary: A representative reconstruction that separates local OCR collection from deterministic, era-aware evidence analysis.

use.practicalQuestion: How can a local document-evidence workflow keep OCR provenance, negation, era-specific term weighting, and a visual orientation artifact inspectable?
use.changedAbility: A collaborator can review captured text, reproduce ordered term evidence, inspect a seeded visualization, and replace prior output only through an explicit recovery-aware action.
readers: AI collaborators implementing or reviewing evidence-extraction workflows
Technical practitioners evaluating provenance, determinism, and recovery

provenance.description: Participant-account-supported reconstruction of a 2018–2019 workflow using realistic synthetic reviewed-OCR material.
provenance.temporalScope: The account describes a method practiced during 2018–2019; this implementation was authored as a current portable exemplar.

technicalVeracity.basis: Focused tests exercise normalization, negation retention, review standing, locator-safe captured-source identity, deterministic ordering and rendering, explicit replacement, and retained-output recovery in the pinned environment.

execution.runtime: Python >=3.12,<3.13; local OCR additionally requires a Tesseract executable

commands.name: run
commands.establishes: Produces ordered term evidence, a seeded word-cloud orientation image, and digest-bearing render metadata from the reviewed synthetic capture.

commands.name: test
commands.establishes: Exercises the artifact's deterministic, provenance, negation, authority, and recovery contracts in the resolved environment.

commands.name: lint
commands.establishes: Returns focused Python syntax, import, correctness, modernization, and maintainability diagnostics.

environmentNotes: The ordinary analysis and test route consumes reviewed text and does not require Tesseract.
The optional OCR route records the locally observed Tesseract version and input digest before analysis.
Repeated-render byte equality is asserted within one resolved environment; cross-platform image-library differences remain an observation boundary.

reviewQuestions: Can a reviewer inspect what OCR produced before weighting begins?
Does every visualization remain connected to ordered machine-readable evidence?
Can an existing accepted-looking output survive a failed replacement?
decisionRules: Treat captured OCR as observed input and require human review before interpretation.
Retain explicit negation terms even when the general stop-word source includes them.
Require explicit replace authority and stage a complete result before promotion.

semanticMarkers.meaning: Source-digested capture, visible negation, era-aware weights, and a visualization paired with evidence.
An opaque script that combines collection, scoring, interpretation, and overwrite into one uninspectable action.
Reviewable capture, deterministic staging, and explicit output replacement preserve the recovery route.

instructionYields.instruction: Separate environment-observed collection from deterministic analysis through a digest-bearing intermediate.
Inspect the ordered JSON before using the word cloud as an orientation surface.
Preserve the prior output until the staged successor is complete and promotion succeeds.

practice.codeExemplarGranularity: One self-contained workflow with two explicit stages, one synthetic capture family, focused tests, and a visitor-readable technical boundary.
practice.complexityAndAllocation: Text normalization occurs once, the sparse TF-IDF matrix is fitted once, era views reuse the matrix, and rendering consumes only the bounded combined term set.

boundaries.evidence: The checks establish current code behavior with the committed fixture and resolved lock; they do not establish equality with an earlier production system, OCR accuracy on an unseen corpus, or interpretive importance of a frequent term.
boundaries.trust: The fixture is realistic synthetic material and the historical method is supported by a participant account rather than recovered operational source.
boundaries.transfer: A receiver selects its own corpus, OCR review policy, stop-word source, era model, privacy boundary, and interpretation method before adaptation.

failureModes: Missing analysis dependencies stop before output staging.
Malformed or empty captures stop before term weighting.
An existing output rejects implicit replacement.
A failed staged promotion restores the prior output when it was moved aside.
recoveryMoves: Resolve the committed lock and rerun the same command.
Review and repair the capture as a distinct input artifact.
Choose a new output path or grant explicit --replace authority.
Inspect the retained output and sibling staging path before another replacement attempt.

relationships.reason: A selected visitor excerpt can point technical readers to this complete versioned implementation after publication acceptance.
The real instance supplies pressure for the first exact-version artifact contract and hosted retrieval route.

practitionerProbePressure.answerRange: A probe may later distinguish five levels of response sophistication; this code sample instead records the implemented technical core and instruction yield.
